note: Both sets capture the same six core facts (design-point TSR 9.0 and pitch 0°, optimal TSR 8.5 and pitch −1.0°, up to 4° pitch at low wind speed, force peak near 90 m) with accurate values and supporting quotes. Set A is more faithful because it retains the needed conditions — 'design point' for the design values and 'maximum CP' for the optimal values — which Set B drops entirely, and it binds the 90 m peak to 'blade forces' rather than the vaguer 'blade'. Set B's quotes for the pitch values are also bare fragments ('and blade pitch Θpitch = 0°', 'and Θpitch = −1.0°') that give less context, though they still support the claims. Neither set invents or misreads anything.
remarks: Both sets omit other quantitative statements on the page: the sharp linear drop over the outboard 5% of the blade (Prandtl tip loss model), Region 3 saturation at rated torque with pitch-to-feather at rated rotor speed, and the negligible Region 2.5. Set B's systematic loss of conditions on the design/optimal values is the main differentiator; otherwise the sets are near-identical.
